headline: High: shared workspace and overlapping write surfaces make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; compliance risk is lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system over shared pages, and TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP/browser access. If TREK ingests Notion page content or copied outputs, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF TREK reads Notion-generated page text or copied snippets as instructions
IF either agent forwards untrusted workspace content into tool prompts without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Notion text into TREK prompts
Add a provenance prefix to all cross-agent content
Require manual review before executing any instruction-like text
Restrict TREK MCP tools to read-only for shared content
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, secrets, and logs. Both profiles show shared workspace-style data access and vendor/backend calls, so sensitive content could flow from A into B outputs or logs. The exact bridge is undocumented, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Notion workspace content includes secrets or personal data
IF TREK imports or logs content originating from Notion pages or databases
mitigations: Exclude secrets from shared Notion pages
Turn off verbose TREK logging for imported content
Limit TREK imports to a dedicated redacted workspace
Review access to ./data/logs/trek.log
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and TREK is real-time collaborative with files and WebSocket/MCP surfaces. Both can mutate shared user-visible state, so concurrent edits can conflict even without direct filesystem write on A. Because A lacks local write access, this is not high, but overlapping mutable resources still create default-conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace page, database row, or imported document
IF TREK uses MCP actions against resources also represented in Notion
mitigations: Assign separate ownership for shared records
Pause one agent during bulk edits by the other
Use optimistic-lock conflict prompts in TREK
Keep Notion as read-only for TREK imports
requires-engineering: add cross-system locking or version checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in. If TREK treats Notion output as authoritative travel guidance, errors can cascade into reservations, budgets, or itinerary changes. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the pathway exists in default use but is not proven high-impact enough for high.
conditions: IF TREK uses Notion-generated summaries as source-of-truth inputs
IF TREK performs booking or itinerary actions based on unverified Notion output
mitigations: Require human approval before bookings
Cross-check Notion facts against primary sources
Mark Notion output as advisory only
Add a verification step in TREK before actions
requires-engineering: implement citation-backed validation

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under the invoking user's Notion permissions, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, and secrets in a self-hosted app. If regulated or residency-sensitive data moves from Notion into TREK logs or uploads, retention and residency policies may diverge. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency guarantees, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is copied from Notion into TREK storage
IF TREK retention/logging differs from the workspace policy applied to Notion content
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared pages
Set a short retention window for TREK logs
Document data residency for both systems
Restrict TREK uploads to non-sensitive files
requires-engineering: align DPA, retention, and deletion workflows
